claim: Infinitely wide, deep, fully-connected neural networks with i.i.d. priors over parameters are exactly equivalent to Gaussian processes.
stance_target: N5: infinite-width networks ARE Gaussian processes
scope_conditions: Fully-connected deep networks, i.i.d. weight/bias priors, infinite-width limit
quoted_support: It has long been known that a single-layer fully-connected neural network with an i.i.d. prior over its parameters is equivalent to a Gaussian process (GP), in the limit of infinite network width...In this work, we derive the exact equivalence between infinitely wide deep networks and GPs.

claim: SGD-trained finite-width neural network accuracy approaches that of the corresponding NNGP as layer width increases -- an empirical, monotonic width-to-GP convergence result.
stance_target: N5 adversarial reading: finite-width nets converge toward GP-like (smooth) behavior as width grows, so a finite ensemble's departure from smooth GP behavior is a width artifact
scope_conditions: MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification, fully-connected networks, varying layer width
quoted_support: We additionally find the performance of the best finite-width NNs, trained with a variant of SGD, approaches that of the NNGP with increasing layer width.

claim: The best-generalizing neural networks in practice are the widest, and the limit of infinite network width is not a disadvantage relative to finite-width representation learning.
stance_target: N5 adversarial reading: wider (closer to GP) is better, undercutting a jaggedness-as-intrinsic-property story
scope_conditions: CIFAR-10, 180 fully-connected 5-hidden-layer networks with varying width
quoted_support: The similarity of the performance of the widest NN in Figure 1 with the NNGP suggests that the limit of infinite network width, which is inherent to the GP, is far from being a disadvantage. Indeed, in practice it is found that the best generalizing NNs are in fact the widest.

claim: The NNGP's predictive uncertainty estimate is highly correlated with prediction error.
stance_target: N5: whether the GP-limit posterior's uncertainty behaves well, relevant background for surrogate-quality arguments
quoted_support: In our experiments, we observe that the NNGP uncertainty estimate is highly correlated with prediction error (Figure 3).

claim: Lee et al. never construct a finite ensemble of independently trained networks and measure the smoothness of its posterior mean as a function of ensemble size K or width -- the paper compares exact NNGP inference to point-estimate SGD-trained networks, not to ensembles.
stance_target: N5/N6: scope boundary -- this paper does not test the specific ensemble-posterior-jaggedness claim
